uncited: It sets itself apart from siblings like [Chunk-based World Streaming](2369-chunk-based-world-streaming.md) by explicitly maintaining a capacity-bounded resident set and using a scoring function to select which blocks to keep in VRAM, rather than simply streaming all visible blocks or using a fixed eviction policy.
*   **Resident Set $\mathcal{R}_t$:** A set of block identifiers currently in VRAM.
*   Assign a small quota of slots to cover visible blocks from each camera in the next batch.
*   If $|\mathcal{K}_{t+1}| > C$, a pure global Top-C selection may leave some views in a mini-batch under-covered.
A selection policy that ensures coverage for all cameras in a batch before filling remaining slots with globally high-scoring blocks.
Choose when multi-view consistency is critical and VRAM is limited.
*   **Time and memory complexity:** The residency selection involves computing scores for the candidate pool $C_t$, which is bounded by $|\mathcal{R}_t| + |\mathcal{K}_{t+1}|$.
Sorting and selection are $O(|C_t| \log |C_t|)$ or $O(|C_t|)$ with efficient selection algorithms.

Tide is a residency-aware data transfer policy for out-of-core volume rendering and training that reuses resident blocks across iterations, transferring only incoming resident deltas to reduce PCIe volume under smooth camera motion [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that Tide is a residency-aware data transfer policy for out-of-core volume rendering and training that reuses resident blocks across iterations, transferring only incoming resident deltas to reduce PCIe volume under smooth camera motion. Source [S1] explicitly confirms: 1) TideGS reuses resident blocks across iterations and transfers only incoming resident deltas (Section 'Differential Streaming'). 2) This is done to avoid wasteful full materialization under smooth camera motion. 3) The policy is residency-aware, maintaining a capacity-bounded resident set and using set differences to stream only deltas. 4) Disabling this increases PCIe traffic significantly (0.10 GB/iter to 0.85 GB/iter), confirming the reduction in PCIe volume. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
